message.content:
Below is a quick‑look list of the **federal long weekends** that Canadians enjoyed in 2023.  
(“Long weekend” means the holiday falls on a Friday or a Monday, giving you a 3‑day break that includes the weekend.)

| Holiday | 2023 Date | Day of Week | Long‑Weekend Span (inclusive) | Notes |
|---------|-----------|-------------|------------------------------|-------|
| New Year’s Day | Jan 1 | Sunday (observed Mon 2) | **Jan 1 – 3** | Observed on Monday, so the holiday itself plus the weekend |
| Family Day (Alberta, BC, Manitoba, Ontario, Saskatchewan) | Feb 20 | Monday | **Feb 18 – 20** | Third Monday in February |
| Good Friday | Apr 7 | Friday | **Apr 7 – 9** | Friday holiday + weekend |
| Victoria Day | May 22 | Monday | **May 20 – 22** | Monday holiday + weekend |
| Canada Day | Jul 1 | Saturday | Jul 1 – 2 | Holiday on Saturday – no 3‑day break |
| Labour Day | Sep 4 | Monday | **Sep 2 – 4** | Monday holiday + weekend |
| Thanksgiving | Oct 9 | Monday | **Oct 7 – 9** | Monday holiday + weekend |
| Remembrance Day | Nov 11 | Friday | **Nov 11 – 13** | Friday holiday + weekend |
| Christmas Day | Dec 25 | Monday | **Dec 23 – 25** | Monday holiday + weekend |
| Boxing Day | Dec 26 | Tuesday | Dec 26 – 27 | Holiday on Tuesday – no 3‑day break |

**Key take‑aways**

* The long weekends above are the ones that give you a full 3‑day break (holiday + weekend).  
* Canada Day (Jul 1) and Boxing Day (Dec 26) fell on a Saturday and Tuesday respectively in 2023, so they did **not** create a 3‑day long weekend.  
* If you’re planning trips, the dates in bold are the ideal windows for a quick getaway.  

Feel free to plug these dates into your holiday‑planning app!
